entry.title: Research Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: This batch is anchored by the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin, the deepest Hermes-specific coverage in the set: a lead walkthrough of the end-to-end pipeline architecture (Hermes drives the plugin, which runs the unmodified official Claude Code CLI) paired with a security-focused companion piece on authentication, where credentials stay entirely with the official CLI via claude auth rather than API keys — directly addressing the top trust question for adopters. Core Hermes news is Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21, released 21 Sep 2026), which adds the --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL — an immediately actionable feature for automation and scripting workflows. Ecosystem context rounds out the section: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 (tagged 18 Sep 2026) hardens MCP security with sessions scoped per invocation, relevant to anyone running MCP servers, and the new AgentProto v0.20.0 runtime (22 Sep 2026), an Apache-2.0 TypeScript agentic runtime that lists Hermes as a supported agent. All items are fresh relative to the 2026-09-23 coverage date (all released within the past week), and the ranking preserves a natural newsletter arc: headline integration deep-dive, core release, security follow-up, then ecosystem developments.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Explains the Hermes Claude subscription plugin pipeline end to end: Hermes talks to the plugin, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable with conversation flowing as native stream-json, while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals and compaction. Requirements are Hermes 0.21.4+ and Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 logged in. Each request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools and skills disabled, and a per-request admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request, rejecting native retry attempts locally.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Documents Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21), released 21 September 2026, which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL (one JSON object per line) instead of plain text so scripts and pipelines can parse output reliably. Update paths include the hermes update command, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The release also rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Details the authentication model of the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: credentials belong entirely to the official Claude Code CLI via claude auth login, and the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes or prints credential files. No API key is required or sent; the plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint and cloud overrides, naming conflicting variables without exposing values. Status checks are local (claude auth status reads the local store in about 0.3s), and separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Covers the Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 release tagged on GitHub 18 September 2026. Headline changes focus on MCP security: sessions scoped per invocation with requests authenticated against invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives become ZIP-only with digest verification, ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected, and new vector-store connectors arrive for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB plus in-memory and portable filters. Breaking changes include deprecation of the MCP sampling callback.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Reviews AgentProto, an open-source Apache-2.0 TypeScript agentic runtime released 22 September 2026 (v0.20.0) that provides one interface to start, message, watch and stop any coding agent with quality gates before work lands. It integrates 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode and Mastra. The reviewer notes the project is very early, with single-digit GitHub stars and Tier 2 components labeled alpha scaffolding, concluding it is early-adopters-only.
